questions.skill: Solve systems of linear equations in context, including systems with no solution or infinitely many solutions
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A theater sold 340 tickets. Adult tickets cost $12 and student tickets cost $7. Sales totaled $3,255. Write a system and find how many of each kind were sold.
questions.prompt_markup:
A theater sold 340 tickets. Adult tickets cost $12 and student tickets cost $7. Sales totaled $3,255.
Write a system and find how many of each kind were sold.
questions.correct_answer: a + s = 340 and 12a + 7s = 3,255; 175 adult and 165 student tickets
questions.grading_note: Form required: a system and both numbers. 12a + 7(340 - a) = 3,255 gives 5a = 875. Check: 2,100 + 1,155 = 3,255.

questions.skill: Solve systems of linear equations in context, including systems with no solution or infinitely many solutions
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: How many solutions does the system 6x - 4y = 10 and 3x - 2y = 5 have? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: How many solutions does the system 6x - 4y = 10 and 3x - 2y = 5 have? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Infinitely many. The first equation is 2 times the second, so both describe the same line.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the number of solutions and a reason.

questions.skill: Solve systems of linear equations in context, including systems with no solution or infinitely many solutions
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A chemist mixes a 10% acid solution with a 30% acid solution to make 20 liters of a 25% acid solution. How many liters of each are needed?
questions.prompt_markup:
A chemist mixes a 10% acid solution with a 30% acid solution to make 20 liters of a 25% acid solution.
How many liters of each are needed?
questions.correct_answer: 5 liters of the 10% solution and 15 liters of the 30% solution
questions.grading_note: Form required: both amounts, labeled. x + y = 20 and 0.10x + 0.30y = 5. Then 6 - 0.2x = 5, so x = 5.

questions.skill: Solve systems of linear equations in context, including systems with no solution or infinitely many solutions
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: For which value of k does the system y = 3x + 2 and 6x - 2y = k have infinitely many solutions?
questions.prompt_markup: For which value of k does the system y = 3x + 2 and 6x - 2y = k have infinitely many solutions?
questions.grading_note: Substitute: 6x - 2(3x + 2) = -4 for every x, so the equations describe the same line only when k = -4.

questions.prompt: Write the system a + s = 340 and 12a + 7s = 3,255 as a matrix equation AX = B. Give the rows of A.

Give the rows of A.

questions.skill: Solve a system in context with an inverse matrix
questions.standard_level: Precalculus. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Precalculus, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: The matrix with rows [1 1] and [12 7] has determinant -5. Does the ticket system have exactly one solution? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
The matrix with rows [1 1] and [12 7] has determinant -5.
Does the ticket system have exactly one solution? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. The determinant is not 0, so A has an inverse and X = A⁻¹B is the only solution.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.

questions.prompt_markup: The inverse of the matrix with rows [1 1] and [12 7] is (1 ÷ (-5)) times which matrix?
questions.grading_note: For rows [a b] and [c d], the inverse is (1 ÷ (ad - bc)) times rows [d -b] and [-c a].
